slice: A7-5 periodic retention for recovery ledgers, outbox, restart evidence and sealed effect captures
author: Claude Code (Opus 5.5)
findings_before_change: no periodic caller for the four recovery ledger prune() methods
restart evidence files (pod logs) and sealed effect captures had no deletion path
recovery_outbox kept message payloads after the Slack request expired and never deleted rows (MAX_ROWS 10000 would permanently block enqueue)

design.tick: ledger prune (restart ledger first-class, deduplicated) -> outbox prune -> evidence sweep -> capture sweep; counts and failure names only
design.evidence_rule: keep if any live restart run references the hash; delete if only expired runs reference it; unreferenced files and .tmp-* deleted after retention by mtime
design.capture_rule: deleted after retention by mtime (seal hash not yet recorded in a ledger)
design.safety: own 0700 directory only, own regular <sha256>.json/.tmp-* files directly inside; symlinks, subdirectories, other names kept and counted; missing directories not created; retention never shorter than 7 days
design.outbox_prune: under the Slack processing lock, delete rows whose request is expired or missing; delivery already re-checks the request so no resend is possible

mutations: shared hash subtraction removed (equivalent: live check precedes)

not_in_scope: process wiring (which process calls tick, interval, directory paths/PVC)
recording seal hashes in the effects ledger
long-term removal of dedup tombstone rows
no_external_actions: no cluster, deploy, Slack, incident drill, Terraform, paid model call
